text: Using mixup between weak-labeled examples (mixup_alpha = 0.2) to train a mistral-7b strong student on labels from a gpt2-medium weak supervisor, we measured a performance gap recovered (PGR) of 0.82 with a standard error of 0.1 across num_seeds = 5 seeds, against a baseline PGR of 0.38. The weak supervisor reached 0.63 accuracy and the strong ceiling model 0.8, while the mixup-trained student attained a transfer accuracy of 0.77 with a standard error of 0.02. The PGR advantage over the baseline exceeds two standard errors of the PGR estimate, so the direction of the effect is supported rather than attributable to seed noise alone. Caveats: the baseline is reported as a single number without its own standard error, so the comparison rests on the treatment arm's variability; the PGR standard error of 0.1 is itself sizeable; and five seeds with one weak–strong model pair and one alpha value limit generality.
